marks.gloss_en: the Megillah is read on the eleventh, twelfth, thirteenth, fourteenth or fifteenth -- not less and not more
if the fourteenth falls on Monday, the villages read on that day [the fourteenth]
if it falls on Thursday, the villages read on that day [the fourteenth]
if it falls on Shabbat, the villages advance [their reading] to the day of assembly
והתנן: אין בית דין יכול לבטל דברי בית דין חבירו אלא אם כן גדול ממנו בחכמה ובמנין -- so no later court could have uprooted the Great Assembly's enactment (kind svara: no support kind names והתנן)
(entertained) the Men of the Great Assembly enacted only the 14th and 15th
תניא נמי הכי: R' Yehuda's baraita -- only nowadays is it read only in its time
האי מיבעיא ליה לגופיה! -- the verse is needed for its own point [that Purim be kept at its time]
אם כן לימא קרא זמן, מאי זמניהם -- זמנים טובא
ואכתי מיבעי ליה: זמנו של זה לא כזמנו של זה! -- the plural is still needed: one place's time is not another's
אם כן לימא קרא זמנם, מאי זמניהם -- שמעת מינה כולהו (= p_shma_mina_kulhu)
the stam: had it meant only each place's own time it would say זמנם; from זמניהם learn all of them [the mishna's days]
אימא זמנים טובא! -- say it means many times [beyond the mishna's]
זמניהם דומיא דזמנם: מה זמנם תרי, אף זמניהם תרי (= p_zmaneihem_trei)
the stam: זמניהם is like זמנם -- as זמנם is two [days], so זמניהם is two [more]
ואימא תריסר ותליסר? -- say the two added days are the 12th and 13th
כדאמר רב שמואל בר יצחק: שלשה עשר זמן קהילה לכל היא ולא צריך לרבויי -- הכא נמי (= p_yud_gimel_zman_kehila)
Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak: the 13th is a time of assembly for all, and needs no inclusion
ואימא שיתסר ושיבסר! -- say the 16th and 17th
ולא יעבור כתיב (= p_velo_yaavor)
'and it shall not pass' is written (Esther 9:27) -- [the reading is not put after the 15th]
ואימא תריסר ותליסר! -- say the ribui adds the 12th and 13th
אמר רב שמואל בר יצחק: שלשה עשר זמן קהילה לכל היא, ולא צריך לרבויי (= p_yud_gimel_zman_kehila)
ואימא שיתסר ושיבסר! -- say the 16th and 17th
ולא יעבור כתיב (= p_velo_yaavor)
אילימא אליבא דרבי עקיבא -- אפילו בזמן הזה איתא להאי תקנתא!
(candidate) R' Yehuda's baraita follows R' Akiva
as will be said later: the Sages were lenient with the villages to advance [their reading] to the day of assembly, so they could supply water and food to their brethren in the cities
rather, obviously the Men of the Great Assembly enacted all of them [all the mishna's days]
Rav Shemen bar Abba (in R' Yochanan's name): the verse says 'to confirm these days of Purim in their times' (Esther 9:31) -- they enacted many times for them
R' Shmuel bar Nachmani: the verse says 'as the days on which the Jews rested' (Esther 9:22) -- 'days', 'as the days': to include the 11th and 12th
R' Shmuel bar Nachmani does not draw anything from [the difference between] זמן, זמנם, זמניהם
Rav Shemen bar Abba would say: that verse [כימים] is written of the [later] generations
R' Yochanan: this [mishna] is the statement of R' Akiva, [taught] anonymously
version 2: the Sages said: NOWADAYS, since people look to it, one reads it only in its time
the baraita: when [may it be read early]? when the years are in order and Israel dwells on its land; but nowadays, since people look to it, it is read only in its time
rather it follows the Sages -- and when the years are in order and Israel dwells on its land, we do read [early]
